result: For the registered toy coordinates, the high-build/low-use morphology loses below H*(r) and wins above it; increasing revision count shifts the crossover to a longer reuse horizon because its registered revision cost is larger.
scientific_use: Calibrates a morphology phase-boundary concept and shows that dominance can reverse as lifetime ecology/resource coordinates change.
parent_boundary: This is elementary lifecycle/amortization economics, not a new GMI law. Future Track-B phase results must estimate/predict morphology-specific quantities prospectively rather than fit this toy after outcomes.
claim_boundary: No empirical neural-vs-symbolic dominance result is established.
